summary: Read Mitankin–Uhlemann arXiv:2411.02629v3 (JLMS): Thms 1.1–1.7 are Markoff-specific; only Thm 2.15 (≥2 finite-weight boundary components ⇒ WWA fails) is general, and it applies verbatim to ES because X_n: 4xyz = n·w(xy+yz+zx) ⊂ P³ has the same boundary as Markoff (triangle of lines w=0, xyz=0); the non-strict semi-integral HP is trivial there too ((0:0:1:1) ∈ D_1). Formulated the strict question: a primitive point (w:x:y:z) is a solution of 4/(nw) = 1/x+1/y+1/z, so strict Darmon-weight-2 points on D_1 are solutions of ES_{nq²} with the q-part only in x (gcd(q,yz)=1). Computed: for n = 9, 25, 49, 73, 97, 193, 409 such points are abundant (29–308 per q ≤ 13), so for n ≥ 2 the relaxation is vacuous and isolates nothing; at n = 1 (BM-obstructed per BL) Darmon-2 strict points = Type I solutions of odd squares, hence empty by T1 (checked w = 9…225), while Campana-2 points exist (w = 27, 125, 243, 343, 675, 1125). Calibration only: the n=1 obstruction survives exactly the square (Darmon) relaxation, i.e. it is T1; no transferable theorem for ES.
next: none for ES; optional one-line note that Darmon-2 strict points of the n=1 ES pair ⇔ Type I solutions of m² (T1).

summary: BRAINSTORM/invol_topological.md §3 already treats Smith theory: Lemma T (any finite mod-2 principle incl. Smith χ(K^G) ≡ χ(K) reduces to an odd weighted count = the open parity problem of memo (a), and is T1-killed if uniform) and Prop K (the canonical solution complex is homotopic to its incidence graph, parity-blind). Ran the item's first step anyway: complex on all ES words n' = tuv−u−v ≤ P (t,u,v ≥ 2) with faces = words sharing a letter; by the nerve lemma it is ≃ the letter/word incidence graph because two letters determine a word, so it is connected but b₁ = 2·#words − #letters + 1 (P = 5000: b₁ = 204 417; 4|t only: 43 553) — maximally far from ℤ/2-acyclic, for structural reasons that persist for any 'shared letter' face rule. Acyclicity would have to come from a different, p-dependent complex whose involution fixed set is certificates, which is exactly memo (a)'s open odd-count problem.
next: none unless a complex with a proved collapse (shelling) and certificate-valued fixed set is proposed.

summary: The item names no complex or moves, so instantiated it with the two natural fixed-p complexes: K(p) (vertices = denominators, 2-cells = solutions of 4/p; invol_topological.md Prop K) and a 'move' complex (vertices = solutions, edges/triangles = solutions pairwise sharing a denominator), and ran greedy elementary collapses via free faces. For p = 73, 97, 193, 409, 1201, 2521 (f = 6–15 solutions), K(p) collapses to c points (c = 1–5 components; b₁ = 0 at these sizes, consistent with Prop K b₁ = 2f−V+c). The move complex either collapses to the same c points or leaves a few critical cells (p = 73, 409) that only encode which solutions share a denominator. Collapses compress homology computations but cannot create certificates; any existence argument would need a p-uniform complex with a proved non-empty invariant, which is the Smith/parity situation already reduced in invol_topological Lemma T.

Borwein–Choi/xy+yz+zx is already compared with ES exceptional sets in BRAINSTORM/bsG_ternary_weinberger.md (E_W = {2,3,5,6,9,11,14,15,35,105,510} vs idoneal numbers; no fixed class group, so no Weinberger finiteness law) and z31_quadratic_forms.md §4, CONDITIONAL_ES.md ~l.282. Since ES has no failures, the only meaningful version of the step is the squarefree/squareful split of restricted-ES exceptional sets, done by factoring the repo's certified lists: U(n) (BREADTH_Z45.md l.265, n ≡ 1 (4) ≤ 10⁹) fails at all odd squares (squareful, structural T1) plus 105, 3985 = 5·797, 25305 = 3·5·7·241, 978145 = 5·7·27947 (squarefree) and 2961 = 3²·7·47, 111969 = 3³·11·13·29 (squareful); E_W has only 9 squareful. So the squareful part is the square obstruction and the sporadic tail is mostly squarefree (4/6, within the ≈ 0.8 squarefree share of odd n), mirroring A055745's squarefree finite-list pattern, with no extra clustering on square factors.
